propositions: The vocabulary carries two redundant headings (## Success Criteria and ## Acceptance Criteria) for one concept, with all gates pooling and applying a single bar to both, making the split vestigial and harmful to criteria detection and checkability

Success Criteria items written as plain bullets do not count toward the P1 blocking floor, cannot carry operator-attested tags, and are not individually checkable, while Acceptance Criteria items are checkboxes that do count and are verifiable

Collapse requires changes across detector regexes, reviewer prompts, criteria routing index, author guides, generated guide, eval specs, test corpus, and 106 store tickets, sequenced as expand-contract to maintain reviewability during migration

Four live files must retain SC vocabulary as out-of-scope exclusions: plan_review_T2.md (pilot metrics semantics), plan_review_verifier.md/agentic.md (definition-of-done), and completion.py (heading-sense usage)

The epic's acceptance criteria contained unsatisfiable and contradictory requirements that required four amendments: AC1 needed three file exclusions, AC4 needed count-agnostic language, AC5 needed to pin exactly one match rather than zero, and unowned scope gap in completion.py was transferred to remaining story 5f4d
